implement.content:
I added the `wrap` command, its test suite and the README row. I haven't run anything, as instructed, so the code is untested.

- **`lib/cmd_wrap.sh`**: defines `usage_wrap` and `cmd_wrap`, following the same pattern as `cmd_number.sh`. It validates the width before any output with a `case` pattern, not arithmetic, so `0`, `07`, `-3`, `+5`, `abc`, `5x` and the empty string are all rejected. It then runs `lk_check_files` and a single `awk` pass that fills each paragraph greedily and puts one empty line between paragraphs.
- **`tests/t_wrap.sh`**: has a test for each of A1 to A14. A13 runs for every bad width and also checks the second stderr line against the usage line, since `check_error` only reads the first. I also added tests for `-h`, an unknown option, width 1, paragraph separation, line joining and `-` as stdin.
- **`README.md`**: added the `wrap` row to the command table.

I didn't touch any existing file under `tests/`.

Run a single awk program: `awk -v w="$_width" '...' "$@"`. awk reads `-` as standard input and handles files one line at a time, so a final line without a newline is still a line and A12's `alpha`+`beta` joins as two words. Each input line is processed as follows. If NF==0 (a blank line), flush the current paragraph. Otherwise loop over $1..$NF; default field splitting ignores leading, trailing and repeated blanks and tabs. The first word of a paragraph starts `cur`. A later word is appended as `cur " " word` when `length(cur)+1+length(word) <= w`. Otherwise print `cur` and start a new line with the word.

Make flush finish the paragraph by printing any pending `cur`. Print the one empty separator line only before the next paragraph's first output line, tracked with a `started` flag, so there is no leading or trailing empty line. Reset `cur` after each flush. Call flush again in END. Empty or all-blank input prints nothing and exits 0. Every printed line ends in a newline.

A12 writes F1 (`alpha`, no newline) and F2 (`beta\n`) under $WORK, then runs `run '' wrap "$WORK/f1" "$WORK/f2"`. A13 loops over `0 07 -3 abc 5x ''` and also checks line 2 of stderr and the empty stdout, because `check_error` only compares the first stderr line. Do that with `sed -n 2p "$WORK/err"` compared to the usage line, and add a `pass`/`fail` call. Also cover `-h` and the usage line on stderr, a missing -w argument, `-w3`, a width of 1, FILE-unreadable via the conventions suite, `-` as stdin, and `+5`. Add one test that crosses the boundary, such as width = exact fit and width minus one. Make sure the tests fail against a wrong implementation, which means asserting the full stdout with `check`.
Add a `| `wrap` | fill paragraphs to a maximum line width (`-w WIDTH`, default 72) |` row to the README command table, keeping the table aligned.
